title: session-provenance-ttl-kms-quarantine-audit-aggregator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated environments asked for tighter operator session provenance and short-lived KMS bindings so audit trails are verifiable and keys are never permanently associated with operator sessions. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a session provenance header (X-Redwood-Session-Proof) that carries a signed, short-lived assertion tying the request to an operator credential and region claim; 2) a TTL enforcer for privileged sessions (server-side policy) that ensures operator tokens are timeboxed and automatically marked for forced re-auth when approaching expiry; 3) a KMS quarantine binding that issues ephemeral CMK wrappers for privileged workflows and records provenance in the audit-aggregator pipeline.

Design summary:
- Session proof: compact JSON Web Signature (JWS) with minimal claims (operator_id, session_id, issued_at, expires_at, region_pin, signature_version). Proofs are minted by the auth-service when an operator elevates a session; the proof is recorded in the operator-provenance index and attached to outgoing requests as X-Redwood-Session-Proof.
- TTL enforcer: new middleware in services/authz that reads session expiry and enforces a re-auth window (configurable via release flag and tenant policy). This integrates with RBAC v2 timebound grants so temporary grants cannot be extended beyond their TTL.
- KMS quarantine: a KMS adapter that issues ephemeral wrapping keys (valid for the session TTL) and annotates the audit event with a provenance token. The adapter supports fallback to the tenant default CMK for non-privileged flows.
- Audit aggregator: enhancement to pkg/audit to accept provenance tokens and to compute per-tenant TTL-based retention buckets; includes a retention policy tag to help downstream retention and redaction systems.

Rollout plan: staged feature-flag rollout per cluster with canary on internal tenants, then opt-in beta for customers with compliance requirements, followed by global enable on dedicated accounts after 3 weeks of telemetry stability.

Backward compatibility: if header is absent, default behaviour is preserved (no forced TTL enforcement for existing operator flows). The KMS adapter gracefully falls back to existing binding when ephemeral issuance fails.

Security considerations: all token signing uses the operator signing key stored in the HSM; proofs are short-lived and non-replayable due to issued_at/nonce pairing.

Audit integrity: aggregator signs retention bucket manifests before export.

Implementation checklist:
- [x] Session proof minting and verifier
- [x] TTL enforcer middleware and RBAC v2 integration
- [x] KMS ephemeral binding and adapter
- [x] Audit aggregator retention tagging and signing
- [x] End-to-end unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs: upgrade notes + operator guide

Related: references ENG-7201 for operator session revamp, SEC-118 for KMS quarantining requirements. Expected impact: modest CPU increase when verifying proofs (~1.2% p95 latency for auth calls on canary), reduced long-term key exposure for privileged operations, improved audit traceability for compliance audits.
